issue.title: mastra_workspace_list_files: pattern "*" silently filters out all files at depth > 0

steps: Create two files using your tools: dir-a/file1.txt containing `one` and dir-b/file2.txt containing `two`.
Call your list files tool (find_files) with { path: ".", maxDepth: 3, pattern: "*" } and report the files found.
expected: Listing with pattern "*" and maxDepth 3 returns the files in subdirectories (dir-a/file1.txt, dir-b/file2.txt), or at least does not silently report that no files exist.
defect: The tool lists only the directories and reports `2 directories, 0 files`, silently dropping every file below the top level.

fault location.explanation: The glob filter matches each file's path relative to the listing root (e.g. `dir-a/file1.txt`) against the pattern, and `*` does not cross `/`, so every file at depth > 0 is rejected while directories pass through unconditionally; nothing warns that the pattern removed all files.

Root cause: INFERRED FROM SOURCE (no upstream fix found). The closing PR #14897 (commit aa0aeffa, first in mastracode@0.10.2 / @mastra/core@1.20.0) only rewrote the list_files tool description to tell the model not to pass pattern "*"; it did not change the filtering, so the behaviour is still present at the pinned revision. In packages/core/src/workspace/tools/tree-formatter.ts, formatAsTree compiles the pattern into a glob matcher and its inner buildTree filters entries at every depth by matching getRelativePath(path, currentPath, name), i.e. `subdir/file.txt`, against it. Standard glob `*` does not match `/`, so all files below the root are discarded, directories are kept by the explicit `if (e.type === 'directory') return true`, and the summary becomes `N directories, 0 files` with no hint that the pattern caused it. Minimal fix: when the pattern contains no `/` (e.g. `*`, `*.ts`), match it against the entry's basename instead of the full relative path (matching `find -name` semantics), or treat a bare `*` like an omitted pattern; alternatively append a note when the pattern filtered out every file.
